requirements.sourceText: A. Language Proficiency (6 credits) Majors are required to take at least six credits (or the equivalent of one year) of college study of an Asian language at the intermediate level or above. Students who already have a pre-established language proficiency in an Asian language can be exempt from this requirement with approval of the Undergraduate Program Director, and in that case, they should take two additional AAS courses at 200-level or above.

requirements.sourceText: B. Core Courses (9 credits) Majors are required to take three of the core courses to AAS major: AAS 102 - Eastern Religions 3 credits; AAS 201 - Introduction to the Civilization of the Indian Subcontinent 3 credits; AAS 216 - Introduction to Japanese Studies 3 credits; AAS 217 - Introduction to Korean Culture 3 credits; AAS 220 - China: Language and Culture 3 credits; AAS 232 - Introduction to Asian American Fiction and Film 3 credits. Note: Students may substitute courses not listed, with Undergraduate Program Director approval.

Students are encouraged to construct their own analytic focus within the major in consultation with the Undergraduate Program Director. Note: Students may substitute courses not listed under their chosen Area of Focus with Undergraduate Program Director approval. (Areas 1-4 as listed on the page.)

Upper-Division Writing Requirement Students with a major in AAS are required to fulfill their Upper-Division Writing Requirement by successfully completing AAS 401, which is certified WRTD. This proseminar in research design, required all undergraduate majors in AAS, culminates in a research proposal or research paper of at least ten-pages in length. requirements.sourceText: The major in Asian and Asian American Studies leads to the Bachelor of Arts degree. No more than 3 credits with a grade of P (Pass) or S (Satisfactory) may be applied to the major. All other courses for the major must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher. Completion of the major requires 39 credits, including at least 21 upper-division credits.

notes.text: Students may gain first-hand experience of Asian cultures through Study Abroad. Stony Brook offers a summer program in China, Japan, India and Korea and academic year programs in China, Japan, and Korea.

Asian & Asian American Studies Honors Program (not evaluated): majors need an overall GPA of 3.00 and an AAS GPA of 3.50 through the junior year. Students write a senior thesis with a faculty advisor, submit a proposal to the Undergraduate Program Director (deadline April 30 for spring, November 30 for fall), and enroll in AAS 495 for the thesis semester.
Accelerated BA/MA in Global Asias (not evaluated): requires the AAS major, at least U2 standing, and a 3.0 GPA minimum; up to nine graduate credits may count toward undergraduate requirements.

Accelerated BA-Teacher Education/MA (not evaluated): requires the Asian and Asian American Studies major with Teacher Certification, at least U2 standing, and a 3.0 GPA minimum. Chinese, Japanese, and Korean Secondary Teacher Education is listed under the Education and Teacher Certification entry.
Acceptable courses for the major may include, but are not limited to, courses with the following designators: ANT, ARH, CCS, CHI, CLT, ENG, HIN, HIS, JPN, KOR, LIN, PHI, POL, RLS, SKT, SOC, THR.

Minors of particular interest to AAS majors include Anthropology, Asian American Studies, Asian Thought, China Studies, Globalization Studies and International Relations, Health Medicine and Society, History, Japanese Studies, Journalism, Korean Studies, Linguistics, Philosophy, Political Science, South Asian Studies, and Women's and Gender Studies.
